why: A token store keyed by id with an expiry time: generate sets it, renew updates it only while still alive, count tallies alive tokens. The heap week fits if counts are frequent (a min-heap of expiries with lazy deletion), but with 2000 operations a dict scan is enough.
hints: All you need per token is its current expiration time.
Alive at time t means expiry > t. RENEW checks that first, then sets expiry = t + timeToLive.
Dict tokenId -> expiry; COUNT counts entries with expiry > t. For large inputs, keep a min-heap of (expiry, id) and pop stale entries lazily. O(n) per count with the dict.
pitfalls: Expiry equal to the current time is already expired: no renewal, not counted.
RENEW on an unknown or expired token is ignored silently.
Only COUNT produces output; times arrive as strings.
